item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E002","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"A German Marshall Fund assessment reported that Scholz’s Zeitenwende included a €100 billion special security fund intended to meet or exceed NATO’s 2% defense-spending target, purchases of F-35 aircraft, military modernization, increased deployments in several NATO states, and military, financial, and humanitarian support for Ukraine; it stated that implementation remained uncertain and that weapons deliveries had been delayed by arms unavailability, bureaucratic procedures, concerns about Russian gas cutoffs, and political caution.","notes":["The excerpt supports an announced fund intended to meet or exceed the target, not that Germany actually met or exceeded it.","The excerpt says arms were unavailable; it does not expressly establish broader shortages."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0013-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
